messages:
alex: Night handoff from me. Quick summary: saw a latency spike on hosted-api-us-west between 02:12-02:38 UTC. P95s jumped from ~120ms to ~850ms, errors stayed low but tail latency impacted streaming responses. Investigated autoscaler logs and k8s events.

alex: What I did: 1) Scoped to a subset of routes (/v1/chat and /v1/stream) that showed the worst tails. 2) Pinned routing to fallback model variants (redwood-small-v2) for 02:25-02:40 to reduce CPU pressure. 3) Disabled the new aggressive pod rebalancer (temporarily) and raised minReplicas on the inference pool from 2 -> 4. 4) Warmed KV cache on a few canary pods by replaying recent prefixes.

alex: Mitigation notes: pin + increased min replicas reduced p95 to ~180ms by 02:36. Streaming token latency still slightly higher due to cold KV caches; warming helped. No customer-facing errors reported, some users saw slower streams until 02:45.

maria: Thanks — did you see any related node OOMs or driver resets?

alex: No OOMs in node logs, but there were several GPU driver warnings on node-45 and node-46 around 02:14 (NVIDIA driver 530 warnings). I cordoned node-46 and drained one pod; that pod rescheduled to node-52 and warmed successfully.

devon: Any deploys around that time? I see a small infra config apply at 02:10 from the infra-deploy-bot. Could be coincidental.

oncall-bot: deploy infra/config-autoscaler updated by infra-bot at 02:09:57 UTC — rollout succeeded.

alex: Right, the autoscaler policy change was the trigger: it tightened scale-down thresholds and caused thrash under bursty traffic. Reverted the policy to previous values at 02:30.

samir: Actions I took: increased model-eviction TTL from 60s -> 180s on the serving pool to keep hot model weights in GPU memory during churn. Also enabled aggressive prefix cache retention for the next 30m.

maria: Anything I should follow up with infra on Monday?

alex: Yes — open ticket to infra to: 1) audit the autoscaler policy change and add a rollback playbook, 2) check driver warnings on node-45/46 and schedule a maintenance window if needed, 3) validate node firmware and CUDA driver versions across US-West. I attached the short log snippet: ```
02:14:21 kubelet: evicting pod/predictor-1234 - GPU driver warning: cuCtxCreate failed: out of memory
02:14:25 kubelet: pod rescheduled to node-52
02:30:12 autoscaler: scale-down inhibited due to recent traffic spike
```

devon: For follow-ups, I'll add a Canary test that simulates short bursty traffic to validate the autoscaler thresholds. I'll also add a synthetic that checks streaming tail latencies.

samir: Next steps for overnight: leave minReplicas=4 for inference-us-west pool until 10:00 UTC; keep KV cache retention elevated for 1h; monitor p95 and stream token latency. If p95 > 400ms for >5m, rollback to blue region routing and notify oncall.

alex: I'll hand off live monitoring to @maria. Dashboards to watch: hosted-api -> us-west -> p95 latency, streaming token latency, autoscaler events, node GPU warnings.

maria: Acknowledged. I will watch for the next hour and post if anything changes.

devon: FYI I left a quick PR in infra: #827 that adds the rollback playbook and documents thresholds. Please review when you get in.

maria: One more note — a couple of customers pinged support with slow responses but no errors. Support ticket IDs: S-9842, S-9843. I've linked them to this thread.

alex: Thanks. If nothing regresses, I'll remove the manual pins at 06:00 UTC and revert minReplicas to autoscaled baseline.

samir: Tagging follow-ups: @devops for node driver checks, @infra for autoscaler playbook.

oncall-bot: oncall reminder — next shift swap at 06:00 UTC.

maria: Handed over. Leaving Slack notifications on for p95 alerts. :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks team — leaving channel. Good night. :sleeping:
